# tfcensus move apply

<WritesState stores="S3,DynamoDB" />

apply plans and verifies each pending block like plan, then asks you to type the block's last
destination unit path (its from path for an in-place block). It checks that no state changed since
it was read, pushes the destinations and then the source with terragrunt run -- state push (so
terraform takes the lock and checks lineage and serial), and records the S3 version IDs in each
unit's &lt;key&gt;.tfcensus-migrations.json. Blocks already applied are skipped.

A native block writes moves\_tfcensus\_&lt;block&gt;.tf into each unit (import blocks in destinations,
removed blocks in the source), then plans each unit to check the files. It changes no state and
no history; run mark-applied after your normal apply.

apply needs bucket versioning (S3-VER). Exit codes: 3 when a block is rejected, 4 when the backend
credentials fail, and 2 for a file or flag error, or with no terminal and no --yes.

## Usage

```sh
tfcensus move apply <migration-file> [flags]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Required | Repeatable |
|---|---|---|
| `migration-file` | yes | no |

## Flags

| Flag | Description | Type | Default | Values | Config key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--block` | run only these blocks (default: all, in file order) | list, repeatable |  |  |  |  |
| `--force` | overwrite moves\_tfcensus\_&lt;block&gt;.tf files of native blocks | bool |  |  |  |  |
| `--repo` | repository root that the file's unit paths are relative to | string | `.` |  |  |  |
| `--var` | set var.NAME in the migration file, as NAME=VALUE | string, repeatable |  |  |  |  |
| `--yes` | don't ask for confirmation | bool |  |  |  |  |

The [global flags](/cli/global-flags) work with every command.

## Output formats

`--format` accepts `tty`, `plain`, `json`, `sarif`. Without it, the format is `tty` when stdout is a terminal and `plain` otherwise. Formats are described on the [global flags](/cli/global-flags) page.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The command finished. With --fail-on, nothing matched. |
| 1 | The command failed: a read, a write, a child process or a check failed. |
| 2 | Wrong usage: an unknown command or flag, a bad value or argument, an invalid config file, or a prompt with no terminal. |
| 3 | A --fail-on gate matched. The report is still written. |
| 4 | Credentials were missing or rejected for every source the command needed. |
| 130 | Interrupted by Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or a cancelled context. |

All codes are listed on the [exit codes](/reference/exit-codes) page.

## Examples

```sh
tfcensus move apply migrations/split_network.hcl
tfcensus move apply migrations/split_network.hcl --block split_network --var env=prod
```
